Build Walkable Graph Network from Street Data

Source: R/network.R
walk_build_network.Rd

Converts user-supplied or downloaded spatial street data into a clean, pedestrian-routing graph structure. Computes edge travel times at a constant walking speed, optionally performs geometric repairs (planarization, endpoint snapping) at the user's discretion, and prepares Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) topology via compiled Rust.

Usage

walk_build_network(
  data,
  crs = NULL,
  walk_speed_kmh = 4.5,
  repair = FALSE,
  planarize = FALSE,
  snap_tolerance_m = 0,
  keep_components = c("largest", "all"),
  drop_classes = c("motorway", "trunk"),
  drop_subclasses = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

An sf object with LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING geometries.

crs

Optional target metric CRS (e.g. EPSG:32722). If provided and data is in a different CRS, it will be projected.

walk_speed_kmh

Walking design speed in km/h (default is 4.5 km/h, the international pedestrian planning standard, approx. 1.25 m/s).

repair

Logical. If TRUE, applies the requested topological cleaning (planarize, snap_tolerance_m). If FALSE, preserves geometry exactly as provided.

planarize

Logical. If TRUE and repair = TRUE, splits crossing lines at intersections to create valid routing junctions.

snap_tolerance_m

Numeric. Threshold in meters to snap endpoint gaps. Default is 0.0 (no snapping). A value between 2.0 and 5.0 is recommended for imperfect street databases.

keep_components

Character. Either "largest" (default) to extract the main connected pedestrian network, or "all" to retain disconnected fragments.

drop_classes

Character vector of road classes to exclude (e.g. c("motorway", "trunk")). Only applied if a class or highway column is present in data.

drop_subclasses

Logical. If TRUE, drops non-network subclasses like sidewalk, crosswalk, cycle_crossing, driveway, and parking_aisle if metadata exists.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints a summary of network construction.

Value

A walk_network S3 object containing:

nodes

sf point collection with node coordinates and IDs.

edges

sf line collection with length_m, travel_time_s, from-node, to-node.

csr

List with Compressed Sparse Row topology arrays (head, to, wt, wl, comp).

walk_speed_kmh

The walking speed used.

giant_comp_id

ID of the giant connected component.

crs

The coordinate reference system of the network.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Standard usage with user data:
net <- walk_build_network(
  data = mis_calles,
  crs = 3116,
  repair = TRUE,
  snap_tolerance_m = 5.0,
  keep_components = "largest"
)
} # }
